title: Linkability of repeated telemetry submissions from the same wearer
description: Continuous submission of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps from the wearable to the device process can allow records across time to be linked to the same individual or routine, even if direct identifiers are minimized. Persistent device identifiers, stable transmission patterns, and location-time traces increase the ability to correlate sessions and reconstruct habits.
assumptions: The wearable/device process stores or forwards telemetry with a persistent identifier, account binding, or otherwise stable pseudonym.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement from standard LINDDUN linkability decomposition; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from telemetry and location data
description: The telemetry in this flow includes GPS position and timestamps, which can directly or indirectly identify the wearer by revealing home/work locations, commuting patterns, or unique movement signatures. Combined with heart-rate and activity patterns, the data may enable singling out a specific person.
assumptions: The receiving process can access sufficiently precise location and time data, alone or in combination with other available data.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode is inferred from general LINDDUN identifiability guidance rather than the retrieved snippets.

title: Detectability of sensitive states or events from continuous sensing
description: Even before full identification, the presence and pattern of telemetry uploads may reveal that a person is wearing the device, exercising, sleeping, traveling, or visiting particular places. GPS and timestamped sensor activity can make sensitive behaviors or events detectable to observers of this flow.
assumptions: An observer can inspect the content, metadata, timing, or frequency of this data flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id chosen by best judgement; detectability subnode may differ in the exact LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: User may be unaware of the extent of personal data shared by continuous wearing
description: By merely wearing the device, the user may not realize that continuous operation captures and transmits detailed heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps. The user may underestimate the granularity, persistence, and sensitivity of the resulting behavioral and location profile.
assumptions: The device interface, onboarding, or notices do not clearly explain continuous collection and sharing of these telemetry categories.

title: Insufficiently informed or specific consent for continuous telemetry collection
description: This flow involves continuous collection of health/activity and location data, which are sensitive and potentially unexpected in scope. If consent is bundled, vague, or obtained without clear explanation of continuous GPS and timestamp collection, the processing may not meet consent requirements or other lawful-transparency obligations.
assumptions: The system relies on consent or similar user agreement for this collection and does not provide sufficiently granular choices or clear notice.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subnode is inferred from common LINDDUN Pro compliance branches; precise node id may vary by catalog version.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive personal data through the telemetry flow
description: The flow contains sensitive personal data, including health-related measurements and precise location history. If the transmission is exposed to unauthorized parties or over-collected relative to purpose, it can disclose intimate information such as health condition, routines, and whereabouts.
assumptions: The flow is accessible to components, operators, or attackers beyond what is strictly necessary, or protections such as minimization and secure transmission are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in the sensitivity of the data on this flow; exact disclosure subnode is selected by best judgement.

title: Excessive disclosure of precise location and activity history during sync
description: The wearable sync sends exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps to the companion app. Precise GPS traces combined with timestamps can reveal home/work locations, routines, and sensitive habits beyond what may be strictly necessary for basic app functionality. This creates an avoidable explicit disclosure risk if the full fidelity of location history is transferred by default rather than minimized.
assumptions: The companion app does not strictly require full-resolution GPS traces and persistent device identifiers for every sync operation, or could operate with reduced precision / selective sync.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for a data-minimization / unnecessary disclosure branch; retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree.

title: Identifiability through persistent device identifier and rich sensor metadata
description: The synced batch includes a device id together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. Even if user account data is not in this specific flow, the persistent identifier and spatiotemporal pattern can identify or single out the user when correlated within the app or with other datasets.
assumptions: The device id is stable across sessions and accessible to the companion app, and the app can associate it with a user profile or other records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; applicability of Identifiability to this flow is strong because stable identifiers plus location/time data are directly identifying.

title: Linkability of multiple exercise sessions and locations across time
description: Because the wearable sends repeated batches containing the same device identifier, timestamps, and GPS traces, the companion app can link separate sessions and movements to the same individual over time. This enables construction of longitudinal behavior profiles even if each batch is viewed independently.

title: Detectability of user activity and app usage from sync events
description: The occurrence, timing, size, or frequency of syncs from the wearable to the companion app can reveal whether the user exercised, traveled, or actively used the device/app, even before inspecting full content. This makes the presence of specific user behaviors detectable from the flow metadata itself.
assumptions: The app or intermediaries can observe sync timing/volume metadata, and syncs correlate with user activities such as workouts.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; threat is grounded in metadata observability rather than payload content.

title: Unawareness of the scope and sensitivity of synced sensor data
description: Users may not realize that syncing transfers not only workout summaries but also precise GPS traces, timestamps, and a persistent device identifier to the companion app. If the app does not clearly explain this scope, users may be unaware of the extent of collection and downstream inferences possible from the data.
assumptions: The companion app's notices or UI do not clearly and granularly explain what is synced and why.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; Unawareness is located at the receiving process because transparency and notice are typically implemented there.

title: Sync collects more personal data than necessary without granular consent or control
description: If the companion app automatically receives full exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, and timestamps whenever sync occurs, users may lack meaningful choice over optional categories such as precise location history. This can create non-compliance risk with data minimization, purpose limitation, and consent/transparency obligations.
assumptions: Precise GPS traces or persistent identifiers are optional for some app purposes, and users are not offered granular controls or lawful-basis-aligned choices.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; strong substantive fit, but compliance depends on jurisdiction and actual consent/control design.

title: User may be unaware of how sensitive health-related entries will be used or shared
description: The wearer manually enters calorie intake, meals, and weight data into the companion app. These entries can reveal health status, habits, and lifestyle patterns. If the app does not clearly explain purposes, downstream sharing, retention, or profiling based on these entries at the moment of collection, the user may share personal data without adequate awareness.
assumptions: The app collects and processes these entries beyond transient display, and notices or just-in-time explanations may be insufficient or absent.

title: Collection of detailed nutrition and weight data may exceed what is necessary
description: The companion app receives detailed meal, calorie, and weight entries from the user. If the app requests or stores more granularity than needed for its stated purpose, or reuses the data for secondary purposes such as analytics or marketing, the collection and processing may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.

title: Sensitive dietary and weight entries may be disclosed to unauthorized parties

title: Repeated meal and weight logs can enable profiling and inference about the wearer
description: Even though the user enters the data voluntarily, longitudinal calorie, meal, and weight records can be analyzed to infer health conditions, dieting behavior, pregnancy, religious practices, daily routines, or other sensitive attributes. The app’s receipt and processing of this flow therefore creates an inference risk beyond the explicitly entered values.

uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is based on best judgement for inference from collected personal data; numbering may vary.

title: Nutrition and weight entries can be linked to the wearer’s identity or account
description: The companion app is likely associated with a persistent user account, device identifier, or wearable profile. As a result, manually logged meals, calories, and weight entries can be linked to a specific individual and correlated with other app or wearable data, reducing anonymity and increasing privacy impact.

description: The mobile app writes detailed health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to persistent storage. If the app stores more granularity, history, or categories of health data than strictly necessary for the service purpose, this flow creates an avoidable disclosure of sensitive personal data into the health log store.

Because these records are privacy-relevant personal data, loss of integrity can misrepresent the user and affect downstream inferences or decisions.

title: Linkability of multiple health events within the store
